- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >1.0) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates price spikes in the 30-day horizon — especially after strong positive sentiment — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast peak.  
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if sentiment shows clear reversal, forecast should adjust earlier than true outcome.  
- In 30-day forecasts, model often overpredicts early in the horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) — reduce initial forecast values by 0.3–0.8% to align with observed lag.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.5 → -1.5 → +1.5), model tends to misalign with true price — apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average.
